clauses.text: These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks -Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: A. Short Title and Commencement

clauses.text: These Directions shall come into effect immediately upon issuance.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: A. Short Title and Commencement

clauses.text: These Directions shall be applicable to Commercial Banks (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'banks' and individually as 'bank').
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: For the purpose of these Directions, 'Commercial Banks' means banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: These Directions are applicable for digital payment products and services provided by the bank as detailed below:
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: Any digital payment product or service offered by the bank to customers for carrying out financial transactions or non-financial transactions such as balance enquiry, set/change Personal Identification Number (PIN), mobile banking registration, generation of one-time password (OTP), ministatement, facility of checking transaction status, and option to the customer to raise dispute/grievance.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: Such digital payment products and services offered directly by the bank or through a system operated by RBI or a system operated by any of the RBI authorised Payment System Operators, and the associated IT assets (applications, systems, infrastructure) shall be considered for the scope of these Directions.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: The following definitions are sourced from Financial Stability Board (FSB) Cyber Lexicon unless explicitly mentioned otherwise.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Availability' - Property of being accessible and usable on demand by an authorised entity.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Confidentiality'  Property that  information  is  neither  made  available  nor disclosed to unauthorised individuals, entities, processes, or systems.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Cyber' Relating to, within, or through the medium of the interconnected information infrastructure of interactions among persons, processes, data, and information systems.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Cybersecurity' Preservation of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information,  and  /  or  information  systems  through  the  cyber  medium. In addition, other properties, such as authenticity, accountability, nonrepudiation, and reliability can also be involved.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Cyber-attack' Malicious attempt(s) to exploit vulnerabilities through the cyber medium to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorised access to assets.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)' A denial of service that is carried out using numerous sources simultaneously.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: ( Source : adapted from ISACA glossary)
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Framework'  A  framework  is  a  structured  set  of  strategies,  policies, procedures, methods, and best practices that guides organisational activities, enables governance, and supports the achievement of defined objectives.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Information System' Set of applications, services, information technology assets, or other information-handling components, which includes the operating environment and networks.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Integrity' Property of accuracy and completeness.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Malware' Software designed with malicious intent containing features or capabilities that can potentially cause harm directly or indirectly to entities or their information systems.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Penetration  Testing'  A  test  methodology  in  which assessors typically working under specific constraints, attempt to circumvent or defeat the security features of an information system.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Phishing'  A  digital  form  of  social  engineering that attempts to acquire private or confidential information by pretending to be a trustworthy entity in an electronic communication.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Vulnerability' A weakness, susceptibility, or flaw of an asset or control that can be exploited by one or more threats .
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Vulnerability Assessment (VA)' Systematic examination of an information system or product to determine the adequacy of security measures, identify security deficiencies, provide data from which to predict the effectiveness of proposed security measures and confirm the adequacy of such measures after implementation.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: The Board of Directors shall approve the policies related to digital payment products and services.
clauses.reason: mandatory disclosure obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Role of the Board :: A. Board Approved Policies

clauses.text: Such policies shall be reviewed at least annually by the Board.
clauses.reason: mandatory compliance requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Role of the Board :: A. Board Approved Policies

clauses.text: The bank shall formulate a policy for digital payment products and services with the approval of its Board.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The contours of the policy, while discussing the parameters of any 'new product' including its alignment with the overall business strategy and inherent risk of the product, risk management/mitigation measures, compliance with regulatory instructions, and customer experience, shall explicitly cover payment security requirements from Functionality, Security and Performance (FSP) angles such as necessary controls to protect the confidentiality of customer data, and integrity of data, and processes associated with the digital product/services offered;
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The policy shall require that every digital payment product/service offered addresses the mechanics, clear definition of starting point, critical intermittent stages/points and end point in the digital payment cycle, security aspects, validations till the digital payment is settled, clear pictorial representation of digital path, exception handling, signing off of the above requirements, mechanism for carrying out User Acceptance Tests (UAT) in multiple stages before roll-out, sign off from multiple stakeholders [post User Acceptance Tests (UAT)], and data archival requirements.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The Board and Senior Management shall be responsible for implementation of this policy.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The policy shall be reviewed at least annually.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall clearly articulate the need for an external assessment of the entire process including the logic, build, and security aspects of the application(s) supporting the digital product or service.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall incorporate appropriate processes into its governance and risk management programs for identifying, analysing, monitoring, and managing the specific risks, including compliance risk and fraud risk, associated with the portfolio of digital payment products and services on a continual basis and in a holistic manner.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The Senior Management of the bank shall have appropriate performance monitoring systems/key performance indicators for assessing whether the product or service offered through digital payment channels meets operational and security norms.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: As part of this process, the bank shall define product-level limits on the level of acceptable security risk, document specific security objectives, and performance criteria including quantitative benchmarks for evaluating the success of the security built into the digital payment product or service;
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall have trained resources with necessary expertise to manage the digital payment infrastructure.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: Wherever the bank is dependent on third-party service providers, adequate oversight and controls for monitoring the activities of the third-party personnel shall be put in place.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall conduct risk assessments with regard to the safety and security of digital payment products/services and associated processes as well as suitability and appropriateness of the same vis-à-vis the target users, both prior to establishing the service(s) and regularly thereafter.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall maintain database of all systems and applications storing customer data in the payment ecosystem and comply with applicable Payment Card Industry (PCI) standards in each of the systems (notwithstanding mandatory requirements of certification/standard accreditation).
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall evaluate the risks associated with the chosen technology platforms, application architecture, both on the server and client side.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall develop sound internal control systems and take into account the operational risk before offering digital payment products and related services.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that its digital payment architecture is robust and scalable, commensurate with transaction volumes and customer growth.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The Information Technology (IT) strategy of the bank shall ensure that a robust capacity management plan is in place to meet evolving demand.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The bank shall have necessary capacity, systems, and procedures in place to periodically test backed-up data and applications pertaining to digital products/services to ensure recovery without loss of transactions or audit-trails.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: A. Governance and Management of Security Risks

clauses.text: The communication protocol in the digital payment channels (especially over internet) shall adhere to a secure standard.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: Web applications providing the digital payment products and services shall not store sensitive information in Hyper-Text Mark-up Language (HTML) hidden fields, cookies, or any other client-side storage to avoid any compromise in the integrity of the data.
clauses.reason: process or procedure with customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: The bank shall implement Web Application Firewall (WAF) solution and DDoS mitigation techniques to secure the digital payment products and services offered over internet.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: The key length (for symmetric/asymmetric encryption, hashing), algorithms (for encryption, signing, exchange of keys, creation of message digest, random number generators), cipher suites, digital certificates, and applicable protocols used in transmission channels, processing of data, and for authentication purposes shall be strong.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: The bank shall adopt internationally accepted and published standards that are not deprecated/demonstrated to be insecure/vulnerable and shall ensure that the configurations involved in implementing such controls are compliant with extant laws and regulatory instructions.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: The bank shall renew its digital certificates used in the digital payment ecosystem well in time.
clauses.reason: process or procedure with customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: The mobile application (mobile banking/mobile payment applications of the bank) and internet banking application shall have effective logging and monitoring capabilities to track user activity, security changes, and identify anomalous behaviour and transactions.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: B. Other Generic Security Controls

clauses.text: The bank shall implement multi-tier application architecture, segregating application, database and presentation layer in the digital payment products and services.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall follow a 'secure by design' approach in the development of digital payment products and services.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall explicitly define security objectives (including protection of customer information / data) during requirements gathering;
clauses.reason: definitional, background, or explanatory clause with no direct compliance action required.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: For digital payment applications licensed by a third-party vendor, the bank shall put in place a source code escrow arrangement or other arrangements for ensuring continuity of services in case the vendor defaults or is unable to provide services.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall conduct security testing including review of source code, Vulnerability Assessment (VA) and Penetration Testing (PT) of its digital payment applications to assure that the application is secure for putting through transactions while preserving confidentiality and integrity of the data that is stored and transmitted.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The VA shall be conducted at least on a half-yearly basis; PT shall be conducted at least annually.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: Testing related to review of source code / certification shall be conducted / obtained and shall be continued annually, if changes / upgrades have been made to the application during the year.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: Penal provisions are included in third-party contractual arrangements for any non-compliance by the application provider.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank may also run automated VA scanning tools on a continuous / more frequent basis to automatically scan all systems on the network that are critical, public facing or store customer sensitive data.
clauses.reason: definitional, background, or explanatory clause with no direct compliance action required.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall compare the results from earlier vulnerability scans to verify / ascertain that vulnerabilities are addressed either by patching, implementing a compensating control, or documenting and accepting the residual risk with necessary approval and that there is no recurrence of the known vulnerabilities.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The identified vulnerabilities shall be fixed in a time-bound manner.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that vulnerability scanning is performed in authenticated mode either with agents running locally on the system to analyse the security configuration or with remote scanners that are given administrative rights on the system being tested.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall verify and thoroughly test the functionality (to validate whether the system meets the functional requirements / specifications) and security controls of payment products and services before their launch / moving to the production environment.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The server at the bank's end shall have adequate checks and balances to ensure that no transaction is carried out through non-genuine / unauthorised digital payment products / applications and the authentication process is robust, secure, and centralised.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The security controls for digital payment applications shall focus on how these applications handle, store, and protect payment data.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) for secure data storage and communication shall be implemented and used correctly in order to be effective.
clauses.reason: definitional, background, or explanatory clause with no direct compliance action required.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall refer to standards such as OWASP-Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (OWASP-MASVS), OWASP-Application Security Verification Standard (OWASP-ASVS), and other relevant OWASP standards, security and data protection guidelines in ISO 12812, threat catalogues and guides developed by National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) (including for Bluetooth and Long-Term Evolution (LTE) security), for application security, and other protection measures.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall redact / mask customer information such as account numbers / card numbers / other sensitive information when transmitted via SMS / emails (including attachments).
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: C. Application Security Life Cycle

clauses.text: The bank shall implement, except where explicitly permitted/relaxed, multifactor authentication for payments through electronic modes and fund transfers, including cash withdrawals from ATMs/micro-ATMs/business correspondents, through digital payment applications.
clauses.reason: Clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: At least one of the authentication methodologies shall be dynamic or non-replicable.
clauses.reason: Clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure to design and implement robust multi-factor authentication methods to act as a strong fraud deterrent; be more difficult to compromise; protect the confidentiality of payment data; and enhance confidence in digital payment by effectively addressing various cyber-attack mechanisms like phishing, keylogging, spyware/malware, and other internet-based frauds targeted at the bank and its customers.
clauses.reason: Clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The implementation of appropriate authentication methods shall be based on an assessment of the risks posed by the bank's digital payment products and services. The risks shall be evaluated in light of the type of customer (e.g., retail/corporate/commercial), the customer transactional requirements/pattern (e.g., bill payment, fund transfer), the sensitivity of customer information and the volume, value of transactions involved.
clauses.reason: Clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The bank shall implement multi factor authentication and alerts (through channels such as SMS and email) for all payment transactions (including debits and credits), creation of new account linkages (addition/modification/deletion of beneficiaries), change in account details or revision to fund transfer limits.
clauses.reason: Clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: As an integral part of the multi factor authentication architecture, the bank shall also implement appropriate measures to minimise exposure to middleman attack which is more commonly known as a man-in-the-middle attack (MITM), man-inthe browser (MITB) attack or man-in-the application attack.
clauses.reason: Clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that an authenticated session, together with its encryption protocol, shall remain intact throughout the interaction with the customer. In the event of interference or in case of closure of the application by the customer, the session shall be terminated, and the affected transactions shall be resolved or reversed out.
clauses.reason: Clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The bank shall set down the maximum number of failed login or authentication attempts after which access to the digital payment product/service is blocked.
clauses.reason: Clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The bank shall have a secure procedure in place to re-activate the access to blocked product/service. The bank shall notify the customer of failed login or authentication attempts.
clauses.reason: Clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: D. Authentication Framework

clauses.text: The bank shall document and implement the configuration requirements for identifying suspicious transactional behaviour, including rules, preventive and detective controls, mechanism to alert customers in case of failed authentication attempts, and the applicable time frames.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: E. Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall parameterise and monitor system alerts in terms of various applicable parameters.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: E. Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: Such parameters, as applicable could include: Transaction velocity (e.g., fund transfers, cash withdrawals, payments through electronic modes, and addition of new beneficiaries) in a short period, more so in the accounts of customers who have never used mobile app / internet banking / card (depending upon the type of payment channel), high risk merchant category codes (MCC) parameters, counterfeit card parameters (e.g., String of Invalid Card Verification Value (CVV) / PINs indicates an account generation attack), new account parameters (excessive activity on a new account), time zones, geo-locations, IP address origin (in respect of unusual patterns, prohibited zones / rogue IPs), behavioural biometrics, transaction origination from point of compromise, transactions to mobile wallets / mobile numbers / Virtual Payment Address (VPAs) on whom vishing fraud or other types of fraud is / are registered / recorded, declined transactions, and transactions with no approval code.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: E. Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall conduct fraud analysis to identify the reason for fraud occurrence and determine mechanism to prevent such frauds.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: E. Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall educate the staff, especially in the fraud control function, about frauds and train them in the following skills and areas of expertise: fraud control tools and their usage; investigative techniques and procedures; cardholder and merchant education techniques to prevent fraud; scheme / card operating regulations; data processing and analysis, liaising or communicating with law enforcement agencies; and the requisite skills required to (i) set and update appropriate rules, (ii) monitor the exceptions thrown based on the rules on a continuous basis and take necessary actions promptly, (iii) communicate / escalate wherever required to appropriate authorities, and (iv) differentiate false positives from the rest.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: E. Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall maintain updated contact details of service providers, intermediaries, external agencies, and other stakeholders for coordination in incident response. The bank shall put in place a mechanism with the stakeholders to update and verify such contact details. The bank shall also formulate specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to handle incidents related to payment ecosystem to mitigate the loss either to the customer or the bank.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: E. Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: A real-time / near-real-time [not later than 24 hours from the time of receipt of settlement  file(s)]  reconciliation  framework  for  all  digital  payment  transactions between the bank and all other stakeholders
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: F. Reconciliation Mechanism

clauses.text: The bank shall also have a mechanism to monitor the implementation and effectiveness of such framework
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: F. Reconciliation Mechanism

clauses.text: The bank shall incorporate secure, safe, and responsible usage guidelines and training materials for end users within the digital payment applications.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: The bank shall make it mandatory for the customer to go through secure usage guidelines (in the customer's preferred language) while obtaining and recording confirmation during the on-boarding procedure in the first instance and first use after each update of the digital payment application or after major updates to secure and safe usage guidelines.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: A mechanism shall be put in place to keep this information periodically updated.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: Customer dispute handling, reporting, and resolution procedures, including the expected timelines for the bank's response, shall be clearly defined.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: The bank shall educate customers about the need to maintain the physical and logical security of their devices accessing digital payment products and services.
clauses.reason: definitional, background, or explanatory clause with no direct compliance action required.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: This shall include but not be limited to recommending secure and regular installation of operating system and application updates, downloading applications only from authorised sources, and having anti-malware / anti-virus applications on devices.
clauses.reason: definitional, background, or explanatory clause with no direct compliance action required.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that its customers are provided information about the risks, benefits, and liabilities of using digital payment products and related services before they subscribe to them.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: The bank shall also inform the customers clearly and precisely on their rights, obligations, and responsibilities on matters relating to digital payments, and any problems that may arise from its service unavailability, processing errors, and security breaches.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: The terms and conditions including customer privacy and security policy applying to digital payment products and services shall be readily available to customers within the product.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation, but has no hard penalty or deadline attached.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - General Controls :: G. Customer Protection, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanism

clauses.text: All digital channels shall be offered on express willingness of customers and shall not be bundled without their knowledge.

clauses.text: The bank shall follow various payment card standards [over and above Payment Card Industry-Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) and Payment Card Industry-Software Security Framework (PCI-SSF)] as per Payment Card Industry (PCI) prescriptions for comprehensive payment card security as per applicability / readiness of updated versions of the standards such as:
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: With reference to paragraph 69(1), though formal certification may not be mandatory, the bank shall follow these standards holistically, as per applicability.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that terminals installed at the merchants for capturing card details for payments or otherwise are validated against the PCI-P2PE program to use PCI-approved P2PE solutions and
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: PoS terminals with PIN entry installed at the merchants for capturing card payments (including the double swipe terminals) are approved by the PCI-PTS program.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall implement the following controls at the HSMs: The HSMs shall have logging enabled and the logs must themselves be tamper proof.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall mitigate the risk of single point of failure at HSM by implementing 'clustering' for high availability and ensuring secure backups.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure access to the HSM through Access Control Lists (ACLs).
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall maintain separate ACLs for each individual application to ensure application-level isolation.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall manage and monitor access to HSM using a robust Privileged Identity and Access Management solution.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure decryption and validation of keys, PIN at HSM.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure card PIN generation and printing directly at system connected to HSM.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure generation and validation of CVV at HSM.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that HSM is implemented with secure PIN block format with controls to disable outputting PIN block in weaker format.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure secure key management for HSMs, including Local Master Keys (LMKs).
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure proper security for the maintenance of physical keys of the HSM.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure the following for improving the security posture of the ATM: implement security measures such as Basic Input / Output System (BIOS) password, disabling Universal Serial Bus (USB) ports, disabling auto-run facility, applying the latest patches of operating system, and other software, terminal security solution, time-based admin access;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall implement anti-skimming and whitelisting solution;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall upgrade all ATMs with supported versions of operating system.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure robust surveillance / monitoring of card transactions (especially overseas cash withdrawals) and setting up of rules and limits commensurate with its risk appetite;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall take up with the card network and/or ATM network, to put in place transaction limits at card, Bank Identification Number (BIN) as well as at the bank level. Such limits shall be mandatorily set at the card network switch itself. Limits may be mandated for domestic as well as international transactions separately;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall put in place transaction control mechanisms with necessary caps (restrictions on transactions), if any of the limits set as per the above requirement is breached. A periodic review mechanism of such limits set as per the risk appetite of the bank shall be put in place as per the Board-approved policy;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall institute a mechanism to monitor breaches, if any, on a 24x7 basis, including weekends, and holidays and put in place a robust incident response mechanism to mitigate the fraud loss, on account of suspicious transactions, if any;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that card details of the customers are not stored in plain text at the bank and its vendor(s) locations, systems, and applications;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that the processing of card details in readable format is performed in a secure manner to strictly avoid data leakage of sensitive customer information.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank using card data scanning tools to identify unencrypted (clear text) payments card data in its ecosystem especially during audits, shall adhere to the following safety measures: any tool (procured by / from a third-party) for the purpose of scanning of unencrypted card data shall first be tested in a test environment to understand the scope and impact of the tool's capabilities;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank using card data scanning tools to identify unencrypted (clear text) payments card data in its ecosystem especially during audits, shall adhere to the following safety measures: the scanning tool shall be installed only in the bank's premises on its devices;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank using card data scanning tools to identify unencrypted (clear text) payments card data in its ecosystem especially during audits, shall adhere to the following safety measures: card data scanning shall not be done remotely;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank using card data scanning tools to identify unencrypted (clear text) payments card data in its ecosystem especially during audits, shall adhere to the following safety measures: discovered data, if any, shall reside in the scanning tool;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank using card data scanning tools to identify unencrypted (clear text) payments card data in its ecosystem especially during audits, shall adhere to the following safety measures: exportable card data shall be appropriately masked (no data, even masked, shall be taken out of the bank's premises / infrastructure);
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Card Payment Security Controls :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank using card data scanning tools to identify unencrypted (clear text) payments card data in its ecosystem especially during audits, shall adhere to the following safety measures: service providers shall be provided limited access to conduct the scan or analyse the data, and such access shall be provided only on the bank's devices.
